tr: „You don't have many jackets. — Only two.“
en: „You don't have many jackets. — Only two.“

tr: „Only two, and both are black.“ — yenisi mavi.
en: „Only two, and both are black.“ — the new one is blue.

tr: „I don't have much time — the store closes at six.“
en: „I don't have much time — the store closes at six.“

tr: Bir kazak iade ediliyor. Değişim mi, para iadesi mi?
en: A sweater is being returned. An exchange or the money back?

tr: İndirim ilanını oku: hangi renk var, hangi fiyattan?
en: Read the sale ad: which colours there are and at what price?

tr: Ödediği kadar: „Thirty dollars… Here is your money.“
en: As much as she paid: „Thirty dollars… Here is your money.“

tr: „Tomorrow is my mother's birthday.“ — iyelik „-'s“ ile.
en: „Tomorrow is my mother's birthday.“ — possession with „-'s“.

tr: „I'm going to visit my parents.“ — şehirde yürüyen Kaan.
en: „I'm going to visit my parents.“ — the one walking in the city is Kaan.

tr: Ali iş sonrasını anlatıyor. Neyi seviyor, neyi sevmiyor?
en: Ali talks about his time after work. What does he like, what does he not like?

tr: Mağaza cümlelerini yaz. Sonunda alışveriş formunu doldur.
en: Write the sentences for a store. At the end, fill in the shopping form.

tr: „It's too small. What size is it?“ — büyük olan gri ceket.
en: „It's too small. What size is it?“ — the big one is the second jacket.

tr: „On Friday I meet my friends.“ — pazartesi parkta yürüyor.
en: „On Friday I meet my friends.“ — on Monday he walks in the park.

tr: „On Sunday we are closed.“ — cuma açık, on otobüsün saati.
en: „On Sunday we are closed.“ — open on Friday, ten is the time of the bus.

tr: Doğum günü hediyesi seçiliyor. Hangi fikir neden eleniyor?
en: A birthday gift is being chosen. Which idea drops out, and why?

tr: „Jackets: black or blue.“ — yeşil ve sarı kazakların rengi.
en: „Jackets: black or blue.“ — green and yellow are the colours of the sweaters.

tr: Beğeni ve iade cümlelerini yaz. Sonunda iade formunu doldur.
en: Write sentences for liking and returning. At the end, fill in the return form.

tr: „It's eighty dollars.“ — bu yüzden Kaan daha ucuzunu istiyor.
en: „It's eighty dollars.“ — that is why Kaan asks for a cheaper one.

tr: „Our store is open every day.“ — her gün açık, yani pazar da.
en: „Our store is open every day.“ — open every day, so on Sunday too.

tr: „The office opens early, at eight.“ — dokuz dükkânın açılışı.
en: „The office opens early, at eight.“ — nine is when the shop opens.

tr: Nil renkleri anlatıyor. Hangi renk işe, hangisi hafta sonuna?
en: Nil talks about colours. Which colour is for work, which for the weekend?

tr: „What do you think?“ — fikir sorusu „do“ ile; „how“ ile değil.
en: „What do you think?“ — the question for an opinion takes „do“, not „how“.

tr: „How much is it? Ninety dollars.“ — iki, Sena'nın ceket sayısı.
en: „How much is it? Ninety dollars.“ — two is how many jackets Sena has.

tr: Önce iş, sonra sevdikleri, sonra cuma, en son hafta sonu planı.
en: First the work, then what he likes, then Friday, last the weekend plan.

tr: „I don't like watching television. I prefer reading or walking.“
en: „I don't like watching television. I prefer reading or walking.“

tr: „We open at nine and we close at seven.“ — sekiz ofisin açılışı.
en: „We open at nine and we close at seven.“ — eight is when the office opens.

tr: Mağazada gömlek alınıyor. Renk, beden ve fiyat art arda geliyor.
en: A shirt is being bought in a store. Colour, size and price come one after the other.

tr: „I don't have enough cheese.“ — patates bir kilo, zaman iki saat.
en: „I don't have enough cheese.“ — potatoes a kilo, time two hours.

tr: Önce kendi rengi, sonra iş, sonra hafta sonu, en son kız kardeşi.
en: First her own colour, then work, then the weekend, last her sister.

tr: „No, it suits you. It is perfect.“ — büyük olmadığını da söylüyor.
en: „No, it suits you. It is perfect.“ — he is also saying it is not too big.

tr: „This black jacket is forty dollars.“ — seksen ilk ceketin fiyatı.
en: „This black jacket is forty dollars.“ — eighty is the price of the first jacket.

tr: Renk ve fiyat yaz. Renk sıfatı isimden önce gelir ve hiç çekilmez.
en: Write colour and price. The colour adjective comes before the noun and never changes.

tr: „For work I wear white or gray.“ — kırmızı ve sarı hafta sonu için.
en: „For work I wear white or gray.“ — red and yellow are for the weekend.

tr: „A ring is beautiful, but it is very expensive.“ — güzel ama pahalı.
en: „A ring is beautiful, but it is very expensive.“ — beautiful, but expensive.

tr: „How much are these shoes? Thirty dollars.“ — çoğulda „are“ geliyor.
en: „How much are these shoes? Thirty dollars.“ — the plural takes „are“.

tr: „I am not going to be late!“ — gelecek olumsuzu „not“ „am“den sonra.
en: „I am not going to be late!“ — in the negative future „not“ goes after „am“.

tr: „I'm looking for a shirt.“ — ceket deneme kabininin yanında duruyor.
en: „I'm looking for a shirt.“ — the jacket is next to the fitting room.

tr: „It's too big. Have you got a small size?“ — küçüğünü sonra istiyor.
en: „It's too big. Have you got a small size?“ — she asks for the small one after that.

tr: Ceket deneniyor. Beden ve renk iki kez değişiyor — sonuncuyu yakala.
en: A jacket is being tried on. Size and colour change twice — hold on to the last one.

tr: „She has a green car and a green jacket.“ — renk sıfatı isimden önce.
en: „She has a green car and a green jacket.“ — the colour adjective comes before the noun.

tr: Bir ceket üzerine fikir soruluyor. Beğeni cümleleri art arda geliyor.
en: Someone asks for an opinion about a jacket. The sentences of liking come one after the other.

tr: „I start work at eight and I finish at five.“ — sekiz başlangıç saati.
en: „I start work at eight and I finish at five.“ — eight is the starting time.

tr: „I'd like to come tomorrow… Tomorrow is Friday.“ — iki cevap da doğru.
en: „I'd like to come tomorrow… Tomorrow is Friday.“ — both answers are right.

tr: İş gününü ve sevdiklerini yaz. „like“ sonrası fiil yine „-ing“ alıyor.
en: Write about your work day and what you like. After „like“ the verb takes „-ing“ again.

tr: „I have a few onions, but not many.“ — „a few“ birkaç demek, çok değil.
en: „I have a few onions, but not many.“ — „a few“ means some, not many.

tr: „I have a meeting on Friday with a new group.“ — gün adından önce „on“.
en: „I have a meeting on Friday with a new group.“ — „on“ comes before the name of a day.

tr: „I don't have many ideas.“ — sayılabilen şeyde olumsuzda „many“ geliyor.
en: „I don't have many ideas.“ — with countables the negative takes „many“.

tr: „Nothing special. I'm going to read, watch a film and walk in the city.“
en: „Nothing special. I'm going to read, watch a film and walk in the city.“

tr: Miktar sorularını yaz. Sayılabilene „how many“, sayılamayana „how much“.
en: Write questions about quantity. „how many“ for countables, „how much“ for uncountables.

tr: „It's gray. Black is only in a small size now.“ — siyah olan küçük geldi.
en: „It's gray. Black is only in a small size now.“ — the black one was too small.

tr: „Then I'm going to buy the shirt and the sweater.“ — ayakkabı çok pahalı.
en: „Then I'm going to buy the shirt and the sweater.“ — the shoes are too expensive.

tr: „My favorite is blue, but I don't buy blue shirts.“ — seviyor ama almıyor.
en: „My favorite is blue, but I don't buy blue shirts.“ — she likes it but does not buy it.

tr: „Today I am going to cook for six people.“ — iki saatin ve litrenin sayısı.
en: „Today I am going to cook for six people.“ — two is the number of hours and of liters.

tr: „I'm going to visit my parents.“ — gelecek üç parçalı: am + going to + fiil.
en: „I'm going to visit my parents.“ — the future has three parts: am + going to + verb.

tr: „No, I'm going to take the bus.“ — soru arabayı soruyor, cevap otobüs diyor.
en: „No, I'm going to take the bus.“ — the question is about the car, the answer names the bus.

tr: Bir dükkânın saatleri soruluyor. Açılış, kapanış, otobüs — hepsi ayrı saatte.
en: Someone asks about a shop's hours. Opening, closing, the bus — each at a different time.

tr: Bir iş günü baştan sona. İş kaçta başlıyor, kaçta bitiyor, sonrası ne oluyor?
en: A work day from start to end. When does work begin, when does it end, what comes after?

tr: Önce istek, sonra fiş, sonra karar, en son para. İade hep bu sırayla gidiyor.
en: First the request, then the receipt, then the decision, last the money. A return always runs this way.

tr: „How much time do I have? Two hours.“ — „time“ sayılamaz, o yüzden „how much“.
en: „How much time do I have? Two hours.“ — „time“ is uncountable, so „how much“.

tr: İki kişi hafta sonu planını konuşuyor. Gelecek kalıbının üç biçimi de geçiyor.
en: Two people talk about their weekend plans. All three forms of the future turn up.

tr: Önce dükkânın saati sorulur ve söylenir, sonra otobüsünki. Aynı kalıp iki kez.
en: First the shop's time is asked and answered, then the bus's. The same phrase twice.

tr: „Can I try it on?“ — zamir „it“ iki parçanın ARASINA giriyor, „try on it“ olmaz.
en: „Can I try it on?“ — the pronoun „it“ goes IN BETWEEN the two parts; „try on it“ is wrong.

tr: Geleceği yaz. Üç parça var ve olumsuzu ile sorusu parçaları oynatarak kuruluyor.
en: Write the future. It has three parts, and the negative and the question are built by moving those parts.

tr: Kaan yemek için miktar hesaplıyor. Hangi şey sayılabiliyor, hangisi sayılamıyor?
en: Kaan works out the quantities for a meal. Which things are countable, which are not?

tr: „My favorite is blue, but I don't buy blue shirts.“ — yeşil kız kardeşinin rengi.
en: „My favorite is blue, but I don't buy blue shirts.“ — green is her sister's colour.

tr: „this yellow sweater is cheap — only ten dollars“ — yirmi gömlek, altmış ayakkabı.
en: „this yellow sweater is cheap — only ten dollars“ — twenty the shirt, sixty the shoes.

tr: „Buy a red sweater… I think that is a good idea.“ — yüzük pahalı, çikolata özel değil.
en: „Buy a red sweater… I think that is a good idea.“ — the ring is expensive, the chocolate is not special.

tr: „I like reading, and I don't like listening to the radio.“ — iki cümle karşıt duruyor.
en: „I like reading, and I don't like listening to the radio.“ — the two sentences stand against each other.

tr: „I'd like to return this and get my money back.“ — satıcı renk öneriyor, Ela istemiyor.
en: „I'd like to return this and get my money back.“ — the seller offers a colour, Ela does not want it.

tr: Önce zaman, sonra patates, sonra peynir, en son para. Sayılamayan ile sayılabilen birbirini izliyor.
en: First the time, then the potatoes, then the cheese, last the money. Uncountable and countable follow each other.
